title: Toric Contact Lenses in Pine Beach, NJ | Academy Vision
metaDescription: Astigmatism doesn’t have to rule out contacts. Learn how lenses for astigmatism work and what a contact lens exam at Academy Vision in Pine Beach includes.
h1: Astigmatism-Correcting Contact Lenses in Pine Beach
lede:
If you have astigmatism, you may have heard that contacts won’t work for you, or tried a pair years ago that never seemed quite clear. Lenses made for astigmatism, often called toric lenses, correct the uneven focus it causes, and many people wear them comfortably every day.

Three of the contact lens options at Academy Vision are made for astigmatism. We’ll measure your eyes, talk through your routine and help you find out whether one of them is a good match.

sections.heading: Astigmatism Doesn’t Rule Out Contacts
sections.html:
Astigmatism means the front of your eye, or the lens inside it, curves more steeply in one direction than the other, a bit like a football instead of a basketball. Light can’t come to one sharp focus, so things may look blurry or slightly stretched at any distance, and long reading or screen sessions can leave your eyes tired.

It’s very common and often comes with nearsightedness or farsightedness. The idea that it rules out contacts dates from a time when lens choices were far fewer. Today, soft lenses for astigmatism come in daily and longer-wear designs.

sections.heading: What a Well-Fitted Astigmatism Lens Gives You
sections.html:
• Correction lined up with your eye. Astigmatism has a direction, and a toric lens carries its correction along a matching angle. When the two line up, vision can be sharp rather than almost clear.
  • A lens that stays in place. Toric lenses are shaped to settle back into the same position after each blink, so your vision holds steady as you read, drive or look around.
  • A fit that feels right. Fit, material and how moist your eyes stay all affect comfort, and small adjustments can make a noticeable difference by the end of the day.

sections.heading: What Happens at an Astigmatism Fitting
sections.html:
Here’s what a contact lens exam at Academy Vision includes. With astigmatism, each step matters a little more.

  1. We check your vision and overall eye health.
  2. We take measurements to get the best possible fit.
  3. We evaluate your tear film, since a healthy layer of tears helps lenses stay comfortable.
  4. We fit you with trial lenses so you can feel how they sit and how clearly you see.
  5. We make adjustments based on comfort and clarity.

The trial step tells you the most. A toric lens needs to settle in the right position to do its job, so how it behaves on your eye says more than the numbers on a prescription.

sections.heading: Why It Helps When Your Eye Doctor Knows You
sections.html:
Astigmatism can shift over the years, and so can the way your eyes handle lenses. When the doctor fitting your contacts has seen your eyes before, small changes are easier to spot, and each fitting builds on what has already worked.

For over 40 years, families in and around Pine Beach have trusted Academy Vision with their vision. Dr. Marc Ullman prides himself on managing difficult contact lens fittings, and Dr. Tyler Lesko’s expertise includes specialty contact lenses and complex lens fittings.

sections.heading: A Prescription Alone Doesn’t Tell the Whole Story
sections.html: Wearing lenses that nobody has checked on your eye skips the step that matters most with astigmatism. A toric lens that turns even slightly out of position can make your vision blur or come and go, and that’s hard to sort out on your own. If your current lenses blur when you blink or glance to the side, or you gave up on contacts because they never looked sharp, it’s worth having the fit checked.

sections.heading: Other Contact Lens Options
sections.html:
• Contact lens exams: what to expect, step by step
  • Multifocal contacts: reading and distance vision in a single lens
  • Scleral lenses: larger lenses that rest on the white of the eye
  • Contact lens options: daily and longer-wear lenses

faq.q: Which lenses for astigmatism can I choose from?
faq.a: Our contact lens options include PRECISION1® for Astigmatism, TOTAL30® for Astigmatism and DAILIES TOTAL1® for Astigmatism. Which one suits you depends on your prescription, your eyes and your routine.

faq.q: Will a lens for astigmatism feel different?
faq.a: Many people find it feels much like any other soft lens. It’s shaped a little differently so it can stay in position, but once it fits well, you shouldn’t notice that. If a lens feels uncomfortable or your vision keeps shifting, tell your eye doctor, since a different fit or design may help.

faq.q: My astigmatism is mild. Do I need a special lens?
faq.a: Not always. Some people with mild astigmatism see well in a regular soft lens, while others notice a real improvement with a lens made for astigmatism. Your exam results and how you see in trial lenses help answer that question.

faq.q: What if I have a lot of astigmatism or keratoconus?
faq.a: Higher or irregular astigmatism sometimes needs a different kind of lens. Our Pine Beach eye doctors use scleral lenses to help patients see clearly and comfortably when other options haven’t worked, and keratoconus is one of the conditions they’re often recommended for.

cta.heading: Ready to Try Contacts for Astigmatism?
cta.html: Whether you’re new to contacts or you gave up on them years ago, our optometrists take the time to listen and explain your options. Call us at (732) 978-9306 to schedule a contact lens exam at our office at 90 Atlantic City Blvd in Pine Beach.
